title: Duplexer Module - GPS L5 (1176 MHz) for GPS/GNSS Anti-Jamming Filter
subtitle: Design Validation and Performance Characterization
author: Dr. Hiroshi Tanaka

sections.1_OBJECTIVE: This document describes the design, simulation, and characterization of a Duplexer Module filter targeting GPS L5 (1176 MHz) for GPS/GNSS Anti-Jamming Filter. The filter is designed on AlN on SiC substrate with a target center frequency of 3065.0 MHz and bandwidth of 230.5 MHz. The objective is to validate that the filter meets the required insertion loss, rejection, and linearity specifications for integration into the GPS/GNSS Anti-Jamming Filter module. This design iteration addresses feedback from the previous revision regarding out-of-band rejection improvements and temperature stability.
sections.2_SCOPE:
- Filter Type: Duplexer Module
- Frequency Band: GPS L5 (1176 MHz)
- Application: GPS/GNSS Anti-Jamming Filter
- Substrate: AlN on SiC
- Package: WLP (Wafer Level Package)
- Design Tool: Matlab RF Toolbox R2024b
- Design Center: Newbury Park Design Center

This specification applies to all variants of the Duplexer Module design targeting GPS L5 (1176 MHz). Results are used to qualify the design for mass production release.
sections.3_DESIGN_PARAMETERS:
Center Frequency:       3065.0 MHz
Bandwidth (3 dB):       230.5 MHz
Insertion Loss Target:  <= 3.4 dB
Return Loss Target:     >= 15.0 dB
Out-of-Band Rejection:  >= 24.0 dB
Isolation (Duplexer):   >= 17.0 dB
Q Factor:               14624
Temperature Coefficient:-20.0 ppm/°C
Die Size:               2.5 x 2.4 mm
Wafer Size:             6-inch
Number of Resonators:   11
Electrode Material:     Al
Passivation:            SiO2
sections.4_TEST_PROCEDURE:
1. Open Matlab RF Toolbox R2024b and load the Duplexer Module template project.
2. Define the substrate stack: AlN on SiC with specified layer thicknesses.
3. Set design targets: center freq 3065.0 MHz, BW 230.5 MHz.
4. Run initial EM simulation with 2D mesh density of 20 cells/wavelength.
5. Optimize resonator geometry using gradient descent (target IL < 3.4 dB).
6. Verify coupling coefficients between resonator stages.
7. Run 3D FEM simulation to account for package parasitics (WLP (Wafer Level Package)).
8. Export GDS-II layout for mask fabrication.
9. Fabricate prototype wafers (6-inch, AlN on SiC).
10. Perform on-wafer probing using Keysight N5227B PNA.
11. Measure S-parameters (S11, S21, S12, S22) from 100 MHz to 9195 MHz.
12. Compare measured results against simulation and specification limits.
13. Perform temperature cycling (-40°C to +85°C) and re-measure.
14. Document results and generate summary report.
sections.5_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA:
- Insertion loss at center frequency shall be <= 3.4 dB
- Return loss in passband shall be >= 15.0 dB
- Out-of-band rejection at +/- 346 MHz offset >= 24.0 dB
- Group delay variation across passband shall be <= 10 ns
- Temperature drift over -40°C to +85°C shall be <= 7.7 MHz
- Power handling shall be >= +35 dBm at 1 dB compression
- ESD tolerance >= 500 V (HBM)
- Die yield on qualification lot >= 87%
sections.6_TEST_RESULTS:
Measurement Date:       2024-04-26
Devices Tested:         46
Insertion Loss (meas):  3.15 dB
Return Loss (meas):     17.4 dB
Rejection (meas):       27.4 dB
Isolation (meas):       21.6 dB
Q Factor (meas):        14624
Group Delay Variation:  3.3 ns
Power Handling:         +27 dBm
Die Yield:              89.0%

Result Classification:  CONDITIONAL PASS
sections.7_OBSERVATIONS:
a) The Duplexer Module design demonstrated acceptable performance for GPS L5 (1176 MHz).
b) Insertion loss is marginally above target; electrode thickness optimization recommended.
c) Rejection at near-band offset requires additional resonator tuning.
d) Temperature stability was within specification across full range.
e) No delamination observed after 1000-cycle thermal shock test.
sections.8_CORRECTIVE_ACTIONS:
1. Review near-band rejection margin for worst-case temperature.
2. Re-run EM simulation with refined mesh for better accuracy.
3. Schedule follow-up measurement after design tweak.
